core.title: Name every plan-declared produce/consume artifact in the code that moves it through flow variables
core.given: A product capability document (a plan artifact under the plan root) declares the product capability's data contract — produce[]: artifacts the product capability owns; consume[]: artifacts it takes from other product capabilities — and a module in this stack moves flow variables for that product capability
core.when: the product capability's Cargo-moving code or its declared contract is written or changed
core.then: Name every declared produce[].name and consume[].name artifact in the module(s) where that product capability moves flow variables, so declaration and carried data cannot drift apart.
prefer: Use plan-matching named constants for artifact names at the flow variables call sites, so every get/put names exactly what the plan declares.
If the product capability no longer owns an artifact, correct the plan instead.
Name your modules as you like; no particular filename is required — what matters is that the module moving the product capability's flow variables names its artifacts.
avoid: Plan produce/consume lists diverging from what is actually put/got through flow variables.
Putting a product capability's declared names only in a shared or unrelated module that does not move that product capability's flow variables.
Trying to suppress a finding: this rule's findings are not suppressible.
unless: The repository declares no product capability contract at all (not applicable).
The product capability has no implementation anywhere: an unimplemented feature, not a broken contract; another rule governs it.
core.why: The core capability-contract schema only checks that the contract is well formed; only a per-stack check reading this stack's source and its flow-variable idiom can see whether the code carries the declared artifacts.
evidence: For every product capability document under the plan root with an implementation, each produce[].name and consume[].name string appears in at least one Cargo-moving module.
The stack's capability-contract check reports no findings; the check run (CI) passes — strict, not suppressible.
verification: Read every product capability document found recursively under the plan root (profile: roots.plan); collect produce[].name and consume[].name artifact names; flag any name that no Cargo-moving module names.

The core capability-contract schema validates the document's shape — both produce and consume lists, each entry carrying an artifact name, and produce entries also a contract and a telemetry URN — wherever the plan lives, but cannot know whether the stack's code puts those artifacts into flow variables: that means reading this stack's source and its flow-variable idiom, which only the per-stack check does.

Recognise a product capability implementation structurally — a module that moves artifacts through flow variables, per the profile's flow-variable-call source idiom (profile: idiom.source_syntax#flow_variables_calls) — never by filename; filename-based naming heuristics are exactly the fitted checks to avoid, and consumers may name modules as they like.

Not applicable, deliberately, in two cases: (1) the repository declares no product capability contract — nothing to honour; (2) a contract is declared with no product capability implementation at all — an unimplemented feature, not a broken contract, belonging to whatever rule governs unimplemented plan, since reporting it here would fire on every freshly planned repository. The check judges code that exists against the contract it claims, not the absence of code.
Strict disposition, severity 4: a finding is not suppressible and fails the check run (CI).

Scope of the check: capability-to-module association is not explicit — it verifies only that at least one Cargo-moving module names each declared artifact, not that the naming module is the one that moves that product capability's flow variables.

fires: A product capability document in the plan root declares a produce[] or consume[] artifact name that no Cargo-moving module names, while an implementation of that product capability exists.
A Cargo-moving module is edited and stops naming an artifact its product capability document still declares.
A product capability document gains a new produce[]/consume[] entry while a product capability implementation already exists, and no Cargo-moving module names the newly declared artifact.
doesNotFire: The repository declares no product capability contract at all.
A product capability is declared in the plan but has no implementation anywhere (unimplemented feature, governed by another rule).
A contract entry is added and the Cargo-moving code already names (or is updated to name) that artifact.
Repositories on other stacks: this core is realized per stack, and a realization fires only on its own stack.
Only the shape of the product capability document is wrong (core capability-contract schema validation, not this rule).

profileRequirements.meaning: Path of the root of plan artifacts; product capability documents live below it and the check reads every product capability document found recursively under this root.
The plan-artifact kind that declares the product capability data contract (the product capability document).

The stack's source construct by which a module moves artifacts through flow variables — the executable call form the check uses to recognise Cargo-moving modules structurally (never by filename) and to locate where declared artifact names must appear.
profileRequirements.bunValue: flow-variables.get(name) / flow-variables.put(name, value) method calls on the flow variables passed to the product capability (e.g. in runCapability(step, flow variables): const basket = flow-variables.get(CONSUMES); flow-variables.put(PRODUCES, { confirmed: true, basket });)

profileRequirements.meaning: Languages of production source; the realization's language activation fact draws its values from here — necessary but not sufficient to identify the stack, so the language-scoped activation itself stays in the realization.

bunOnly.text: Plan-matching name constants used at the flow variables call sites: `export const CONSUMES = "orders:priced-basket"; // plan: consume[].name` / `export const PRODUCES = "orders:confirmed-order"; // plan: produce[].name`; in `runCapability(step, flowVariables)`: `const basket = flow-variables.get(CONSUMES); flow-variables.put(PRODUCES, { confirmed: true, basket });`.
bunOnly.reason: The worked example is written in this stack's module/export syntax and flow variables call form; bun.json stays the reference example for other stacks.

neutralityNotes: Flow variables and the product capability produce/consume data contract are ATDD-core concepts, not stack specifics, so they stay in the neutral core. Three things could not be made neutral and remain Bun-only: (1) the stack-identity activation facts (language typescript/javascript — its values supplied by the profile's tooling.languages, since language alone does not distinguish Bun from Node.js or Deno — and change stack_is_bun) — the neutral core is scoped to a stack by its profile instead; (2) this rule's detector, family and finding ids (bun_flow_router_infrastructure, checks/capability_contract_honoured.mjs, declared_artifact_not_named_by_flow_variables_moving_code), which the core's verification describes generically; (3) the concrete fix-hint code snippet and the 'capability.ts' filename illustration, dropped from the core because bun.json is delivered as the worked reference example. Severity 4 and the strict, non-suppressible disposition are kept in core verification per the notProfileKeys policy. The profile's plan root carries the path itself (plan); the recursive plan/** traversal of product capability documents below that root is core verification behavior, with the Bun activation's path_glob kept as the realization's derived form. Recognising a Cargo-moving module structurally needs the stack's flow variables source-call idiom, stored as idiom.source_syntax#flow_variables_calls: these are executable source-code method calls used by the check — a source-syntax fact, not a construct of plan artifacts, so idiom.plan_syntax does not cover them. The realization's language activation values come from tooling.languages, while the language fact itself stays Bun-only because language alone does not identify the stack.
